finding: The same released int8 graph decodes correctly under onnxruntime-node on the CPU EP and degenerates to stray Arabic-script tokens in Chrome. The companion-UI warm-up gate cannot catch this because it only checks non-empty output; this harness does.
candidate_causes: Dynamic-quantization kernels differ between the ORT CPU EP and the WASM EP: the graph is 106 DynamicQuantizeLinear plus 146 MatMulInteger, so EP kernel differences are the leading hypothesis.
Audio preparation differs: the browser path decodes through decodeAudioSourceToMonoPcm with its browser resampler while Node parsed the WAV directly.
next_steps: Re-run with backend=wasm to separate EP from the backend label.
Hash the decoded PCM in the page to prove both sides receive identical audio.
If the EP is the cause, an fp32 self-export is the fix, currently blocked on the omnilingual-asr install and the 1.3 GB checkpoint.
scope: Browser timing evidence for this model is valid; browser transcript parity FAILED rather than being merely unverified.
